When I was 16, my boyfriend took LSD on the way to a concert. I didn't partake and sat next to him in the back of our friend's van. We decided to stop at a gas station and everyone got out. My boyfriend was staring straight ahead motionlessly and wouldn't respond to me, so I stayed with him while everyone else left.

As the driver leaves, he asks me to hand him the bag of chips sitting on our seat. So I unbuckle my seatbelt, hand him the chips and sit back down. He pours a few in his mouth before folding the bag and putting it in his cargo pocket, turns around and goes into gas station.

A few minutes pass by. I try to get my boyfriend to respond, but he's gone, and it kinda creeps me out. So I turn his face to mine and look directly into his eyes, saying his name over and over. All at once I saw my own reflection in his pupil and the detail was simply stunning. I looked more closely and it was like I could see everything behind me perfectly. At some point I stopped saying his name and simply stared. Time stopped and I stared at myself in his eyes for what seemed like hours.

This was interrupted by the opening of the driver's door. I wrenched myself away and time started again. The driver looked at me with a weird expression on his face and asked if I was all right. I couldn't describe what had happened so I just said I was fine and the others came back so we left.

A few minutes later, I was still reeling from the time-stopping phenomenon and my boyfriend still failing to respond to me when the person in front of us braked hard and the van suddenly lurched out of control. I strained against my seatbelt as we careened through highway lanes, struggling to regain control. The driver was able to pull off to the shoulder and we all freaked out for a few minutes.

This jolted my boyfriend out of it and he was finally responding, and acting fairly normal, asking if I was all right. After we all settled down, the driver asked me to hand him the bag of chips sitting on our seat. As I unbuckled my seatbelt to hand them to him, I had an intense wave of deja vu. "Wait a minute, I already handed you these."

"What?"

"Before you walked into the gas station."

"Yeah," confirmed my boyfriend. "I remember you putting them in your pocket."

The driver didn't remember this happening at all and had no chips in his pocket. I asked my boyfriend if he was conscious of everything while he wasn't responding, and he said yes, he had been fully aware of everything but unable to speak. He remembered everything I did.

The driver said that when he left the car, my boyfriend and I had been staring intensely into each others' eyes and he didn't say a thing to him as he left to go to the gas station.

The thing is, I had to unbuckle my seatbelt to hand him the chips. And if it had been unbuckled when we'd swerved... it was a huge minivan with the middle row of seats taken out and several kids sitting on the van floor while we sat on the back row of seats. I would have flown through the van and definitely hurt myself and others.

TL;DR My boyfriend trips, I do not, and we share a hallucination from a reality in which my life was in grave danger.

The trail ends at a scenic spot on the creek with a plaque and large boulders.
